fragments.text: Target edition · 16 October 2026 · US-first · USD.

Oncall owns the full on-call alerting and incident-response job: receive monitoring or phone-in incidents, identify coverage, wake a responder through real phone/SMS/push, escalate until acknowledged, coordinate verified recovery, communicate and finish the follow-up. The first buyer is a US software/IT operations team replacing PagerDuty, Opsgenie / Jira Service Management incident response, or Splunk On-Call (VictorOps). The target also competes with incident.io On-call, Rootly and Resolve AI through integrated response and bounded agent work. This is a destination contract, not a description of what currently ships.
The approved 16 October scope governs these clauses. Release 1 remains hosted coordination beside the existing pager, with production paging OFF.
Writing a target does not activate providers, change the approved UI/homepage or waive the independent standby and real-phone cutover requirements.

Existing IDs remain stable. Clauses OC-001–022 retain release guarantees; OC-023 onward completes the purchased job. A clause is **done** only within its stated limits and cited exercising flow; **partial** names the implemented subset; **missing** has no implementing flow. Acceptance evidence is the public journey required to complete the clause; merely listing it is not a passing run.
The OC-003 and OC-006 policies below authorize scoped machine coordination and explicitly approved signed response events under OC-053, while preserving human-session authority and paging OFF.

**OC-001 — Event identity and alerts.** Persist accepted events separately from alerts and human incidents. Repeated source event IDs return the original receipt; changed bytes with the same identity conflict. A deduplication key groups active alerts only within its source/service/environment; recovery affects the matching alert and never resolves an incident.

**Acceptance evidence:** POST signed and bearer events through /api/ingress/:source; repeat a normalized identity, conflict changed content, send recovery before trigger and after a newer generation, and inspect protected state. Verify grouping across multiple sources without merging service/environment boundaries.
**Status:** partial

**OC-002 — Routing replay.** Retain routing policy version and explanation at admission. Replay is read-only, returns ordered decisions, and produces no alert, incident or external effect. Unmatched signals remain visible and unowned; suppression reasons remain inspectable.

**Acceptance evidence:** Admit a severity-routed event, change policy, POST /api/replay and compare the immutable admission explanation with the proposed decision in submitted order; compare state before/after for zero writes.

**OC-003 — Roles and authority.** Incident changes require an active authorized human session or an explicitly scoped OC-053 service-account capability. A machine is attributed as a service account and never gains human-session, member-management or human-review authority. Viewer reads; responder coordinates; admin manages services/policies/members/import. Ingest credentials grant no read or human authority. Bearer and signed intake return only `duplicate`, stored event `id`, source `eventId`, `service`, `observedAt` and `acceptedAt` (201 accepted; 200 deduplicated). Routing decisions, snapshots and alert identities stay behind authorized read/export doors; scoped OC-053 reads disclose only granted service records, and archive/export authority remains session-protected.
Revocation takes effect on the next request. Every mutation enforces current authority server-side.
The stakeholder role that reads only business-service status and approved updates is specified and tracked in OC-061.

**Acceptance evidence:** Use anonymous, expired, revoked, viewer, responder and admin sessions on reads, commands, sources and archives; revoke or downgrade while a real HTTP mutation is incomplete and prove no publication. Verify minimal intake receipts disclose no private routing data.

**OC-004 — Incident state transitions.** Incident state transitions are explicit. Acknowledgment assigns responsibility. Resolution requires recovery evidence and a summary, independently of alert recovery. Optimistic revision checks reject stale edits. All accepted changes append an attributed timeline transactionally with state. This resolution rule governs declared incidents; an alert-only page that its source recovers closes without a human summary under OC-056.

**Acceptance evidence:** Declare from admitted alerts, acknowledge, reject stale concurrent changes, clear the source alert, refuse resolution without evidence and summary, then resolve and inspect the attributed timeline over HTTP.

**OC-005 — Copied runbooks.** Runbooks are copied into the incident at declaration; future service edits never silently rewrite incident instructions. Follow-ups carry owner, due date, open/completed state and completion evidence. Resolved incidents retain open work and editable review.

**Acceptance evidence:** Declare an incident, edit its service runbook and confirm the copied incident steps remain unchanged; create an owned due-dated action, require completion evidence and retain unfinished work and review after resolution.

**OC-006 — Bounded outbound incident effects.** Only signed OC-053 response events to an endpoint a current administrator explicitly approved may leave the incident workspace in release 1. No paging provider notification, AI call, production action or Lamp publication occurs in release 1. Configured remote mail sends sign-in links only. Handoffs are minimum summaries with stable identity and visibility; exported draft is explicitly unreviewed. Source links grant no access. External acceptance/delivery/acknowledgment are distinct later records.

**Acceptance evidence:** Use coordination and handoff preparation/export on a normal installation with no approved OC-053 endpoint; prove no paging receipt, production action, AI call or external publication occurs. Confirm draft exports remain unreviewed and source links confer no access. Approved OC-053 events are proved under OC-053.

**OC-007 — Native archive.** Native archive preserves services, policies, incident/alert/event/timeline identity and attribution, runbook and follow-up history. Validate schema and references before atomic restore. Invalid restore preserves existing data. Do not export authentication secrets/sessions. Released migrations remain immutable;
verify prior-data transitions.

**Acceptance evidence:** Export through /api/archive; restore valid held records and reject malformed references/storage failures without losing prior data. Inspect event, incident, runbook, action, timeline and attribution identity and confirm authentication material is absent.
**OC-008 — User-authored records kept.** No automatic deletion of user-authored incident records.
Owner export/restore is supported.

Ingress accepts bounded structured fields. Provider and incumbent-compatible intake retain bounded structured evidence and no raw bodies under OC-059. Native Events API parsing is bounded to 64 KiB; authenticated oversized, malformed or incomplete native input retains only its first at most 64 KiB of exact raw bytes as untrusted incomplete custody under OC-059, never parsed or routed from that prefix. Incumbent-compatible endpoints and provider adapters use the larger per-provider bounds of OC-059. No arbitrary remote fetching or runbook execution.
Display user content as text, never HTML.
**Acceptance evidence:** Submit over-limit and malformed intake, hostile structured text and runbook links; verify that no input is parsed or retained beyond its bound and that
unauthenticated or
over-limit command input is refused (native incomplete custody is verified under OC-059), literal display with no script execution/fetch, and preservation of authored history after restart/export.
**OC-009 — Accessible interface.** Keyboard-complete responsive UI, labeled fields, focus-visible controls, status announcements, readable failure states and contrast.

The conformance bar is WCAG 2.2 Level AA for every web surface and, for the OC-029 apps, the same success criteria as they apply to native iOS/Android plus Dynamic Type and Android font scaling to 200%.

Named assistive-technology journeys are VoiceOver with Safari on macOS and NVDA with Chrome on Windows for web, and VoiceOver on iOS and TalkBack on Android for the apps; each completes sign-in, finding an incident in the filtered list (OC-060), acknowledge, snooze, reassign, schedule view and override.

Each release publishes a conformance report (VPAT 2.5 Accessibility Conformance Report, WCAG 2.2 edition) stating the result per success criterion and per surface; an unsupported criterion is named, never omitted.
A failed write is visible and never shown as saved. UI unavailable must not be described as pager coverage failure because stage 1 supplies no pager.

**Acceptance evidence:** At 1440 and 390, use keyboard-only declaration, acknowledgment, notes, schedules, overrides and preview; inspect focus/labels, status announcements, literal hostile HTML and a real stale-write failure with no saved claim. Run axe-core with the WCAG 2.2 A and AA rule sets on every surface at 1440 and 390 in light and dark themes and record zero violations;
complete the named VoiceOver/Safari, NVDA/Chrome, iOS VoiceOver and Android TalkBack journeys for acknowledge, snooze, reassign and schedule view with recorded outcomes;
and publish the release's conformance report before any new target surface ships.
**OC-010 — Health and honest commands.** Health checks storage and

identifies the deployed version, operating commands describe actual local and hosted effects, and acceptance records distinguish local evidence from remote/provider/pilot outcomes. Capacity promises require measured evidence.

**Acceptance evidence:** Run check/describe and /health with storage available and unavailable; compare deployed identity to the actual build. Record local, hosted, provider and human-drill outcomes separately
and test durable failure diagnostics for each new execution class.
**Status:** done

**Implementation evidence:** `src/api.ts`; `src/base/deployment-health.ts`; `OPERATIONS.json`; `tests/runtime.mjs`; `tests/coordination-health.mjs`; `tests/hosted.mjs`; `tests/transfer.mjs`. **OC-010 coordination health, deployment identity and honest command effects survive storage failure** checks the emitted build identity, real database loss (503 with the same identity and no success), recovery with unchanged records, and read-only check/describe through the pinned executable. Hosted-mode production serving checks its supplied source/fingerprint/version separately from the one-time real Cloudflare release evidence in ACCEPTANCE.md. Command declarations distinguish local setup/dev/reset/transfer, provider deployment/removal and dry-run provider reads without writes. No pager health, independent availability, measured capacity or human-drill outcome is claimed.
OC-026/027/028/029 inherit pager/timer/mobile/standby health; OC-064 owns paging measurements.
Every new execution class under OC-030–035, OC-039, OC-045–048, OC-051, OC-053–054, OC-056–058 and OC-063–072 inherits durable failure diagnostics before shipping.
The public intake request keys, authentication modes, field limits, service-ID lookup and a curl example are documented in [Incidents and alerts](docs/incidents.md#send-an-alert-event).

Identity is source + eventId; conflicts compare the normalized allowlisted signal fields (canonical timestamps and trimmed strings), rather than irrelevant JSON whitespace/order or discarded fields. Receipts, admission order, decision snapshot and alert mutation commit atomically. Each signed/bearer source is explicitly scoped to service identities; the service binds its environment.
A routed key (OC-072) selects exactly one service in its allowed scope for each event before identity, deduplication and generation apply.
On the native Events API, lifecycle generation is required: trigger and recovery must carry the same generation.

Incumbent-compatible endpoints whose payloads carry no generation (OC-055) never require one: Oncall derives it from the source's deduplication key and receipt order, as OC-055 specifies, and the same tombstone and reopening rules then apply.

Recovery before trigger creates a recovered tombstone; later trigger for that generation records evidence without reopening. Reopening needs a new generation. A delayed recovery can only close its own generation, never a new alert.

Stage 1 routes coordination ownership, with no timed escalation or paging. Replay returns historical decision/ownership/policy/evaluation snapshot beside the proposed current decision in submitted order; it does not claim schedule replay.
All active members see all workspace incident data. Admin/responder/viewer permissions differ from incident commander attribution.
Any active responder/admin can attest recovery and follow-up evidence; attestation is a human claim, not automatic measurement verification.

Archive and restore require current admin authority; handoffs remain internal. Restore replaces application state while preserving the current administrator identity; credentials remain installation-local, other sessions are revoked, clients reload state. Historical and inactive identities are retained.

The Stage 1 active-member statement covers the admin, responder and viewer roles. OC-061 adds a status-only stakeholder role with no incident, alert, runbook or archive access; its explicit audience and receiving limitations remain in OC-061.

**OC-011 — Calendar-day rotations.** Named-zone calendar-day rotations retain fixed primary/backup member slots. Hand-offs use the wall minute plus integer civil days, not fixed elapsed seconds. Repeated minutes explicitly choose earlier, later or reject; nonexistent/rejected boundaries produce visible gaps. Override intervals include their start and exclude their end; overlap in the same role is rejected. Inactive/viewer/missing members do not shift slots. A duplicated primary/backup assignment leaves backup unavailable.

**Acceptance evidence:** Save primary/backup schedules and query HTTP preview across spring/fall DST, ambiguous/nonexistent minutes, override edges and overlap refusal; retain inactive/viewer/missing slots as gaps and detect duplicate primary/backup responders.

**OC-012 — Paging off.** Production paging is OFF. Every normal-installation delivery attempt refuses with an explanation that an independent standby and real-phone drill are required. No production paging provider sends, synthetic delivery proof, cron delivery, SMS, voice or push are performed. Existing pager is authoritative. Escalation policies are inspectable configuration data, not active timers. A labeled demo simulation is not production delivery or acceptance.

**Acceptance evidence:** On a normal installation POST each delivery/job/tick/callback/resume door and confirm paging-OFF refusal with no receipt. Treat demo simulations as simulations. Native cutover additionally requires OC-026–029 and OC-038 real-phone/provider-failure acceptance.

**OC-013 — Held history stays historical.** Held synthetic job/receipt/callback identities remain historical data. Restore pauses pending jobs. Historical acknowledgment and explicit cancellation retain attribution; resume and new timer starts refuse while paging is OFF. An acknowledgment never proves recovery.

**Acceptance evidence:** Restore held synthetic jobs/receipts/callbacks, observe pending work paused, acknowledge or cancel with attribution, reject resume, and verify incident recovery remains unchanged.

**OC-014 — Side-effect-free previews.** Schedule preview, now/next and replay are side-effect-free; actual historical delivery claims remain labeled synthetic. Nothing in this release certifies production delivery.

**Acceptance evidence:** Read now/next and schedule/routing previews, compare durable state and receipt counts, and confirm no timers or provider actions were created and historical synthetic data stays labeled.
**OC-015 — Strict module archives.** Strict module archive validation and atomic replacement remain supported. Imported pending historical jobs pause. Scope and local capacity limits remain explicit.

**Acceptance evidence:** Round-trip the strict module archive through protected HTTP; reject unknown fields, broken references and injected SQL failure atomically, retain callbacks and pause pending historical jobs.

**OC-016 — Recovery checkpoint.** A paired recovery checkpoint captures coordination and scheduling records with both revisions in one consistent storage snapshot, excludes authentication, and validates its envelope and intrinsic record integrity. Explicit current-admin restore replaces both datasets atomically, pauses imported pending jobs, preserves the current-password mapping rule and revokes prior authority exactly as coordination restore does. Missing references in retained paused/finished history remain evidence, never dispatch authority; missing references for pending jobs are invalid. Invalid input, capacity failures, storage failure or losing concurrent writes preserve the previous complete state and cannot revoke a winning restore's new session. Verify the actual emitted Worker/D1 and private local CLI workflow before claiming this target implemented.

**Acceptance evidence:** Use /api/recovery/checkpoint and the private CLI to capture and restore both revisions; exercise malformed/capacity/storage failures and competing writes, identity mapping, orphan history and session revocation without revoking the winning restore session.

**OC-017 — Reviewed handoffs.** Persist explicitly authored, unsent handoff copy with an explicit intended audience, immutable incident/service snapshots and canonical content hashes. Preparation and review actions have stable identities that conflict on changed content. Only current active responders/admins prepare, review or withdraw; viewers inspect permitted internal records and admins restore. A review binds exact copy and source versions, becomes ineligible on source drift or a recovery hold, and never grants sending, publication, recovery verification or independent-review authority. Withdrawal is terminal and preserves attributed append-only history. Keep OC-006 and historical unreviewed envelopes unchanged. Use separate additive handoff storage/archive bounded to 64 records, 128 history entries per record, 128 KiB per record and 1 MiB aggregate. Explicit checkpoint version 2 includes handoffs; version 1 remains supported. Restore retains historical identities and holds active approvals atomically alongside existing recovery and credential/session safeguards. Invalid input, capacity/storage failure or losing concurrent writes preserve the complete prior state. HANDOFF-STAGE.md defines retained snapshots, eligibility and permissions;
transfer proof exercises the protected HTTP review and restore flow.
No provider send, remote fetch or Lamp publication is authorized.

**Acceptance evidence:** Prepare, review, inspect and export exact handoff copy over protected HTTP; change source/revision, withdraw, restore v1/v2 and race writes. Verify eligibility/holds, stable action identities, append-only attribution and all storage bounds with no send authority.

**OC-018 — Maintained root commands.** Maintained root seed commands use the pinned Base installer, owner identity, dev identity and theme. Ordinary email-link sign-in is kept and tested independently of dev identity. Setup creates no example incident or service. Release 1 supports hosted coordination beside the existing pager without an independent standby; portable SQL batch bindings are required. `rer deploy` verifies deployment identity, claims the configured owner automatically and retires the setup token. Hosted email-link sign-in requires a configured remote mail provider. Removal with the same Cloudflare credentials deletes only recorded deployment resources and verifies that they are gone. On local and hosted apps, the configured owner uses native email links, while admin-created team members use installation-local workspace names and passwords at `/signin/local`; no invitations are sent. Local dev identity never grants hosted access, and anonymous first-admin bootstrap at `/api/setup` remains loopback-only.
**Acceptance evidence:** Exercise documented setup/dev/build/preview/reset/archive/deploy dry-run, owner entry and member password sign-in.
Hosted acceptance must actually deploy, retire setup authority, use a real emailed owner link, coordinate with a member after reload, and remove recorded resources with empty provider readback.

**OC-019 — Additive upgrade.** The additive upgrade removes the one-row coordination store after migrating every entity and original array order to relational tables. Released migrations stay unchanged. Held passwords and identities are preserved. New Base identity cannot silently claim held coordination data.

**Acceptance evidence:** Seed the held one-row SQL data, migrate, sign in with the held password and compare all entities, nested histories and original ordering through HTTP; repeat migration/restart without silent reassignment to Base identity.

**OC-020 — Now/next and calendar feed.** Now/next explains current coverage and each role's next effective hand-off. The private ICS feed uses the same resolved UTC boundaries including overrides/gaps and exports primary/backup separately. It requires a current session; default window is seven days, explicit windows are bounded to 31 elapsed days. Calendar downloads carry no public bearer access. Alert intake records immutable events with scoped source credentials; intake never starts paging.

**Acceptance evidence:** Read now/next and authenticated ICS for seven-day default and bounded explicit windows; verify primary/backup UTC boundaries, overrides and gaps, deny unauthenticated access and confirm admission starts no paging.

**OC-021 — Move-in preview.** Opsgenie then PagerDuty file move-in uses Base import-kit D1. Preview writes zero rows. A current administrator must review the exact source fingerprint before applying. Users are matched by normalized email and grant no login rights; schedules and policy data stay paused. Original bytes, unmapped fields, rejected objects, journal and provenance are retained. Every unmappable rotation/rule is named; no partial rotation approximation is allowed. Missing detail exports reject. No account/API calls or routing credentials are activated.

**Acceptance evidence:** Follow provider export instructions, preview saved Opsgenie and PagerDuty list/detail bundles with zero writes, inspect exact rejected/unmapped rules and fingerprints, apply paused and explicitly map people/services before adopting native coverage.

**OC-022 — Resume and undo.** Journaled imports support bounded resume after restart and explicit undo. SQL checks current actor/session/admin authority inside publication and reversal. Changed source identities conflict; duplicate unchanged sources are idempotent. Undo removes only unchanged attributed native objects; edits are preserved with an explicit conflict. Invalid input or failed publication leaves prior committed state unchanged; partial progress remains visible and resumable.

**Acceptance evidence:** Apply, interrupt/restart, resume and undo both vendor imports over HTTP; revoke authority at publication, inject SQL failure, replay unchanged/changed identities and preserve native edits as named undo conflicts.

Shapes recorded under OC-021 (13 Oct 2026, no requirement reworded): each documented Opsgenie `data` response and each documented PagerDuty list or single-detail response, saved unchanged, one per bundle key or an array of them; PagerDuty layers that ended before the one open-ended layer began, kept as named history; a PagerDuty whole-day layer in a zone with offset changes when the supplied `final_schedule` is equivalent across an offset change. [MOVE-IN.md](MOVE-IN.md) lists the fields and pages read.

Release 1 is hosted incident coordination alongside the team's existing pager. Paging stays OFF, the existing pager stays authoritative, and coordination does not require an independent standby. Hosting does not synchronize the pager's configuration, deliver pages, announce role moves externally or prove delivery. Teams keep their existing pager routes and responder notification settings in place.

Release 2 paging and its independent standby are not built. Its requirements include dual alert intake, configuration pull, independent store/secrets/identity and external role-move announcements; durable absolute deadlines and term-scoped sent markers; one-use acknowledgment at both sites; two channels on two providers per responder; carrier registration; and real-phone and provider-failure drills. Measured takeover-to-page time belongs in this contract only after those drills. None is inferred from coordination deployment or local proof.

**OC-003 / OC-006 policy (21 October 2026, deliberate requirement change; authorized by the OC-053 fleet brief):** The former session-only incident-change requirement now also admits explicit, service-scoped machine capabilities through `/api/v1`. Formerly, routing decisions, snapshots and alert identities were readable only through session-protected doors. A token with the matching read permission now reads its granted services' records, including the incident alert IDs those records carry through the services, schedules, incidents, actions, analytics and integrations families; intake routing-decision records and frozen intake snapshots remain session-only. It has no archive, export or audit door. A `services:write` token may update granted service definitions, which is an administrator action for humans, but cannot create services or widen its grant. The former prohibition on external incident publication now permits only administrator-approved minimal signed response events through the OC-053 outbox. Existing human role checks, human-review acceptance, protected archive/export, minimum intake receipts and paging OFF remain required. Token authority is never inferred to be a human response. A machine acknowledgment must name an active responder, who becomes the incident's commander and assignee. The timeline and audit record it as the service account's act naming that member, never as that member's own acknowledgment. A token cannot accept human-review follow-ups. Completion it supplies under the evidence policy is an automation claim, not a human attestation. Delivery is receiver acceptance, not acknowledgment by a person.

**Security consequences:** Machine keys grant only named API permissions and services; they cannot create sessions or manage members. A key or endpoint acts only while the administrator who created it remains an active administrator. Demotion or removal suspends it from the next request and at dispatch, and its authority never transfers. Endpoint approval declares exact recipients and minimal data fields; installation-local digest/AES-GCM custody, dispatch-time authorization, credential-revision fences, bounded attempts, signed receipts and protected replay apply. Revocation cannot retract bytes already sent; ambiguous outcomes remain uncertain. Restore transfers history without tokens, signing keys, approvals or automatic sends. Erasure severs matching automation labels and local capabilities without rewriting permanent pseudonymous audit facts. Each event body is exactly `operationId`, `type`, `service`, `incident`, `revision`, `state` and `at`, frozen at the domain commit. It carries no names, summaries, notes, evidence URLs or contacts. It is signed with HMAC-SHA256 hex over `timestamp + "." + body`, using a per-endpoint key that is never returned, logged, exported or written to audit. Only an authenticated receiver receipt records `sent`, and an unsigned success is `uncertain`. Recipients are literal globally routable IPv4 HTTPS addresses on port 443, with no hostname, DNS lookup, userinfo, query or fragment. Redirects are never followed. An operation gets at most five attempts. Service-account keys, held as SHA-256 digests, never enter audit or logs. Creating, rotating, revoking and replaying are administrator-only and each commits with its OC-041 audit entry.

**Evidence and gaps:** `tests/runtime.mjs` extends the emitted HTTP journey with `tests/automation.mjs`; `tests/transfer.mjs` and `tests/checkpoint-cli.mjs` exercise populated inactive transfer and erasure; `tests/automation-browser.mjs` exercises the existing settings pattern at 1440 and 390. `tests/automation.mjs` (creator demotion/removal) exercises next-request read/write refusal, separate origin/endpoint/receiver dispatch custody, no transfer to another administrator and refusal after restart; its machine acknowledgment asserts commander/assignee and service-account timeline/audit attribution. These policies record meaning changes, not independent status promotions. Not proved: live receiver/TLS interoperability, hosted scheduling latency, provider delivery, human response or paging readiness. Hostname/IPv6 recipients and a general automation engine are not supplied. Issued releases, CHANGELOG and RELEASE.json remain unchanged; the next release must record both clause amendments.

**OC-023 — Services, teams and ownership.** Maintain searchable services, environments, owning teams, dependencies, escalation policies, responder contacts, runbooks and lifecycle state. An alert exposes its applicable runbook before declaration; declaration keeps the immutable copy under OC-005. Team managers administer their own coverage; private team/service access is enforced on UI, API, exports and integrations. Workspace administrators retain explicit cross-team access. Backstage imports ownership and dependency changes with preview, provenance and conflict review; stale or ownerless services stay visible and cannot silently route to an invented person. Business services built on these dependencies, with stakeholder subscriptions and an internal status view, are OC-061; each service's recent deploys and configuration changes are OC-065.

**OC-041 inheritance:** Team-scoped audit export must commit accepted state with its permanent audit entry and retain a durable failed, interrupted or uncertain outcome on crash or lease expiry before shipping. Its own acceptance proves atomic rollback, subject-erasure-safe export and interruption at the execution boundary.

**Acceptance evidence:** Create two teams and a dependent service through the UI/API, read the alert runbook, import a Backstage ownership change, deny a foreign-team user through direct/export/chat doors, and resolve an ownership conflict without losing incident history.

**OC-024 — Follow-the-sun, PTO and holiday coverage.** Compose primary/secondary layers with daily, weekly, custom interval and business-hour rotations across named zones. Show effective coverage and gaps for follow-the-sun handoffs, US federal/company holidays and individual PTO imported from Google Calendar or Microsoft Outlook with least-privilege consent. A holiday calendar is not a universal US work schedule: teams choose their rules. A proposed schedule change shows who loses/gains coverage, including DST, and cannot silently close a gap or move retained member slots. Overlaps have an explicit precedence and explanation. The moved duty and its acceptance are retained verbatim in OC-026, OC-066.

**Acceptance evidence:** Build New York/Los Angeles/London handoffs, add a US holiday and approved PTO in Google and Outlook, inspect a DST weekend and uncovered interval, then apply a reviewed layer change and compare actual paging targets to the preview. During the New York-to-London handoff, page the London responder through their verified UK voice and SMS routes under OC-066, and see a shift held by a responder with only one verified route flagged as degraded in the preview.
**Status:** partial

**Ruled carve Gap (23 October 2026):** Google/Outlook PTO import may use dated one-time owner-role evidence; it has not been run. Mixed acceptance sentence beginning “During the New York-to-London handoff” stays here because it combines live paging and coverage-preview duties. **OC-025 — Swaps, reminders and calendar subscriptions.** Responders request and accept schedule swaps from web or mobile with explicit substitute acceptance and manager rules; no accepted swap may leave coverage ambiguous. The moved duty and its acceptance are retained verbatim in OC-026. Personal on/off-call reminders obey each responder’s channel/time rules; overdue swap requests remain visible. Support Google Calendar and Outlook through revocable scoped ICS subscriptions as well as authenticated downloads; feeds contain schedule data only and revocation ends access without changing historical assignments.

**Acceptance evidence:** Request, accept and race two swaps, reject an unauthorized substitute, revoke a calendar subscription, view the effective rotation in Google/Outlook, and observe automatic change/reminder delivery plus a visible failed-notification outcome.

The mixed sentence “Personal on/off-call reminders obey each responder’s channel/time rules; overdue swap requests remain visible.” stays here: reminder delivery belongs to OC-027, while overdue swap visibility remains OC-025. The mixed acceptance sentence stays verbatim. Google/Outlook viewing may use dated one-time owner-role evidence; not run. PARTIAL.

**OC-026 — Native US phone, SMS, push and email paging.** Every responder enrolls and verifies real destinations and keeps two separate ordered notification rule sets, one for high urgency and one for low urgency (OC-057), each by channel, on/off-call state and delay in minutes; a rule with zero delay notifies immediately. The two-channel/two-provider requirement below applies to the high-urgency set; the low-urgency set may be, for example, push and email only. Deliver SMS and voice using Twilio and an independently operated second provider such as Telnyx, plus mobile push through APNs/FCM and incident email through a configured US mail service (Resend, SendGrid or Amazon SES). Require at least two channels over two independent providers per responder, including a telephone route independent of the mobile push path. SMS and voice to destinations outside the US follow the OC-066 country list, and this two-channel/two-provider rule applies to every responder in every listed country. Complete US A2P 10DLC registration, sender/caller identity, consent/opt-out handling and carrier testing before activation. Opt-out, invalid number, unregistered sender or failed provider leaves coverage degraded and pages an approved alternate; it never silently counts as delivered. Show queued, attempted, provider-accepted, device/carrier-delivered where observable, human-confirmed and explicitly acknowledged separately, with provider costs/usage in USD.
